title: Vibe coded a cosy game where you explore a tiny globe as a biplane, magic carpet and fishing boat
author: WeAreFictional
selftext:
Hey folks! This is a free web game project that I made using Cursor, running on ThreeJS. It's a submission for VibeJam competition.

[Play now (Recommended for Desktop with Sound)](https://tinyskies.vercel.app)

Tiny Skies is a cosy little (optionally multiplayer) game you can pick up and play whenever you have a few minutes. You can:

\- fly as a biplane, magic carpet, or fishing boat (unlockable via multiple playthroughs)

\- play casual capture the flag with other players

\- shoot paintballs at each other (and at gremlins!)

\- make package deliveries

\- race in mini races

\- catch some fish

\- drift on a magic carpet

\- collect jellyfish friends

\- or if you're up for it, figure out how to save the world from impending doom

I hope you'll enjoy flying (and boating) around the world and soaking in the vibes! Would love to hear your feedback and suggestions in the comments. Thank you!

comments.author: MinimusMaximizer
comments.body: The usual question: What was the asset pipeline? Especially objects and textures? This is really nice.

replies.author: WeAreFictional
replies.body:
Sure!   
\- About 80% of the 3D of all the low poly assets are generated with a mix of Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro by code.   
\- For more detailed 3D assets (e.g the moon, capybara, statue (if you beat the game), they are all created with Tripo3D, I try to make it as low poly as possible  
\- The world/globe is procedurally generated.

comments.author: insats

This is truly impressive!

Most vibe-coded games published on this sub look like, well, something vibe-coded. Slop, in other words.

replies.author: insats
replies.body:
I just had a closer look in the browser (only saw the video on my phone earlier) and now I'm even more impressed. The attention to detail... Cute little sounds, the rain drops on the windshield. You may be good at vibe-coding, but I'd say you're good at making games! :)

I'm also surprised that you've been able to come that far without programming skills because a lot of vibe coded projects end up riddled with bugs and architectural issues that the agents are usually not able to sort out once the project has grown larger.
